summary.one_liner: Janus, Janus-Pro and JanusFlow are DeepSeek's unified multimodal models that handle both image understanding (visual Q&A, formula-to-LaTeX) and text-to-image generation, with code for inference and local demos.
summary.what_it_does: The repository publishes the code and model references for the Janus model family: Janus-1.3B, JanusFlow-1.3B, Janus-Pro-1B and Janus-Pro-7B, hosted on Hugging Face. Janus-Pro is described as an improved version of Janus with a revised training strategy, more training data and larger model size. The Janus models use an autoregressive transformer with decoupled visual encoding paths for understanding and generation. JanusFlow combines an autoregressive LLM with rectified flow for image generation, and its example uses the stabilityai/sdxl-vae decoder. The README gives Python snippets for multimodal understanding (image plus question to text) and text-to-image generation that saves samples to disk. It also describes Gradio demos and, for Janus, a FastAPI server with a test client.
use_cases: Image question answering with a vision-language model
Converting formula images to LaTeX code
Running a local Gradio web demo of image generation
Hosting a FastAPI endpoint for multimodal inference
Research on unified understanding and generation models
how_to_run: pip install -e .[gradio]  # optional local Gradio demo for Janus-Pro
pip install diffusers[torch]  # needed for JanusFlow
notable: Decoupled visual encoding for understanding and generation within one transformer (Janus)
Rectified flow integrated into an LLM without major architecture changes (JanusFlow)
Janus-Pro scales data and model size, with 1B and 7B variants
Multiple model sizes released on Hugging Face with online demos
caveats: Model use is governed by the DeepSeek Model License, separate from the MIT license on the code
Examples assume a CUDA GPU (.cuda() calls) and bfloat16 precision
JanusFlow generation also needs the separate SDXL VAE and the diffusers package
